clue.text: One hopes it won't produce a shock in retirement!

definitions.text: One hopes it won't produce a shock in retirement!

parts.words: One hopes it won't produce a shock in retirement!
parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, and the shock is the kind faulty mains-powered bedding could give a sleeper

explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: bedding warmed by mains power, which a sleeper trusts not to give a jolt once they have turned in.

clue.text: Number three's out

indicators.note: out can mean astray or wrong, so the letters of the word beside it are disordered

parts.note: the fodder is three, its possessive s giving no letter

explanation.surface: The person at number three has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is the old crossword trick: something that numbs, an anaesthetic. 'out' rearranges THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a num-ber is something that numbs, and this gas is an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Doctor tucked into fish and left his ghastly lard

indicators.note: tucked into means placed snugly inside the fish that follows

parts.note: an eel is a fish
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: ghastly means in a dreadful state, so the word before it is disordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor eats fish heartily and leaves the horrible fat behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'lard' as a verb, not the fat: to lard a speech with quotations is to garnish it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to lard prose with ornament is to decorate or garnish it.

clue.text: Merry man's cakes and sweets

definitions.meaning: the fat friar among Robin Hood's band of Merry Men
British schoolchildren's word for snacks and treats, as sold in a school shop

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow's cakes and confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a name and a noun: the friar in Robin Hood's band, and British school slang for snacks and treats.

clue.text: International gallery accepts frame of modigliani is copy

indicators.note: accepts means the international gallery takes the framing letters inside itself

parts.note: the Tate is a group of British art galleries

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its border, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gallery takes in a picture frame once holding a Modigliani, but the painting is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to mimic or reproduce something is to copy it.

clue.text: Class making awful din after start of break

indicators.note: after says the din comes behind the opening letter of break
start of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a racket is a dreadful noise

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren get noisy once break time begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a group or category, as in a tax band or an income group.

clue.text: Toast and tiniest amount of prosciutto in a spread, perhaps

definitions.text: Toast and tiniest amount of prosciutto in a spread, perhaps

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters before it are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the tiniest amount of a word is a single letter, its first

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A little ham on toast as part of a laid-out meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'spread' rearranges TOAST, P (the 'tiniest amount of' prosciutto) and IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Italian starter course often includes bruschetta and a little cured ham laid out on a platter.

clue.text: Guy tours a river for a girl

indicators.note: tours means goes round, so the man's name surrounds the two letters

parts.note: Ken is a man's name, an example of a guy
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A man goes round a river on a girl's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' wraps KEN round A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a female first name.

clue.text: Toy extremely dirty delinquent initially has to carry

indicators.note: initially says the delinquent comes first, ahead of the letters from dirty

parts.note: a Ted was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes, with a reputation for trouble

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to bear a load is to carry it

explanation.surface: A filthy young offender has a plaything to lug about at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' is not a first-letter signal here: it places TED ahead of DY, the letters 'extremely' takes from dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a stuffed cuddly animal is a child's plaything.

clue.text: Grill current composer featured in hello

indicators.note: featured in means the current and the composer appear inside the greeting

parts.note: hi is an informal hello
I is the physics symbol for electric current
J S Bach, the German baroque composer

explanation.surface: An interviewer questions a living composer profiled in a celebrity magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at Hello!, a British celebrity magazine; 'Grill' is the cooking appliance, not an interrogation.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small Japanese charcoal brazier used for barbecuing.

clue.text: Changed key before start of duet

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Musicians switched to a different key before beginning their duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: modified, made different.

clue.text: Fish head off for a stream

indicators.note: head off means the fish loses its first letter

parts.note: a brill is a European flatfish

explanation.surface: Fish turn and make for a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the B from BRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small brook.

clue.text: Fling rag and slate old Vietnamese leader

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth, as a handkerchief is in its short form
to slate and to pan both mean to criticise harshly
Nguyen Cao Ky was prime minister of South Vietnam in the 1960s

explanation.surface: Someone throws down a cloth and criticises a former ruler of Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' reads as a verb beside rag and slate, but it is the noun: a brief affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a fling is a brief affair, and this phrase means sexual dalliance or mischief.

clue.text: The French runner leads with very loud music

indicators.note: leads says the runner goes at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: a ski is a runner, the blade something slides on
FF is fortissimo, the score marking for very loud
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A French athlete heads the field while loud music blares.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a 1950s British style of folk-jazz played on guitars and washboards.

clue.text: Victoria,say, intended to be heartless relation

parts.note: Victoria is one example of an Australian state

indicators.note: to be heartless means the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: meant is the past tense of mean, to intend

explanation.surface: A queen such as Victoria planned to be a cold-hearted relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be heartless' takes the central A out of MEANT. 'relation' is a telling, an account, not a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of telling: an account or recounting of events.

clue.text: Farming method that might produce green fare?

indicators.note: the answer's letters could be rearranged to give the two words that follow, so those words are the fodder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A way of farming that could yield eco-friendly food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that might produce' says the answer's letters can make GREEN FARE, so those nine letters rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a way of keeping poultry and livestock with access to open ground.

clue.text: Will made ready for death

parts.note: Will is not a man's name but a legal document, drawn up before one dies

explanation.surface: A man called Will was prepared for his end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the legal adjective for someone who dies having left valid written instructions for their estate.

clue.text: American has nuts in 11 old beast

indicators.note: in puts the word for nuts inside the answer to clue 11

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 11 across, a small stream
nuts and mad both mean crazy

explanation.surface: An American keeps nuts in an ancient creature numbered eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' stands for the answer to 11 across, RILL, and 'in' puts MAD inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Holmes, perhaps, damaged heel at start of trial

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A detective injured his heel as a court case opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges HEEL AT plus the T that 'start of' takes from trial. Holmes is Dame Kelly Holmes, the British double Olympic champion runner, not Sherlock.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Kelly Holmes is a British Olympic gold-medal runner.

clue.text: One of the greens, new leader entertaining Miliband at the outset

indicators.note: entertaining means having as a guest, so the rearranged word takes a letter inside
new means freshly made, so the letters of the word beside it are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: at the outset takes the opening letter of the name before it

explanation.surface: A Green Party member and new party chief hosts Ed Miliband to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LEADER into EERALD, and 'entertaining' puts M inside it. Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party from 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it names a bright shade of the colour, after the gemstone.

clue.text: Short knickers and slip

indicators.note: short means the word for knickers is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers

explanation.surface: Brief underwear and a petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the final S from BLOOMERS. The slip is a blunder, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in British slang: a blunder or embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Stuff under counter is stiff stuff!

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the word for stuff below the counter

parts.note: a buck is a counter or marker passed round in poker
to ram is to stuff or cram something in

explanation.surface: Goods kept below the shop counter are the hard stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places RAM below BUCK in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a coarse cloth stiffened with size, used in bookbinding.

clue.text: Try old foreign recipe with beans oddly omitted

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters after it take an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: oddly omitted drops the odd-numbered letters, leaving the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Have a go at an old dish from abroad, leaving out the beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly omitted' leaves EN from beans, and 'foreign' rearranges RECIPE with EN into PERIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to try something is to undergo or sample it.

clue.text: Small alien found in mine

indicators.note: found in means the alien sits inside the word for mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A little extraterrestrial is discovered down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the French-derived word for little, used of clothing sizes and in law.

clue.text: Extremely educated lawyer bound old anthology

indicators.note: bound means tied together, so the two pieces are joined side by side
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A very learned lawyer had an old collection of writings bound.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: either of two medieval Icelandic collections of Norse poems and myths.

clue.text: Protection, say, is required after start of attacks

indicators.note: after says the next two pieces follow the opening letter of attacks
start of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: Defences are needed once the attacks begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the shield of Zeus, hence patronage or shelter.

clue.text: Hero relaxed when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the word for relaxed is said out loud and another spelling heard

parts.note: idle means not working, taking it easy

explanation.surface: A hero was at ease when giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person greatly admired or adored.

clue.text: Take top off sauce in a strange country

indicators.note: take top off means the sauce loses its first letter

parts.note: pesto is an Italian basil sauce

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the two short words before it are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Open a jar of sauce in an unfamiliar land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take top off' removes the P from PESTO, and 'strange' rearranges IN A into NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: one of the Baltic states.

clue.text: To droop after wine is a signal to stop

indicators.note: after says the word for droop follows the wine

parts.note: red is a kind of wine
to flag is to tire and droop

explanation.surface: Nodding off after a glass of wine tells you it is time to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the warning banner that halts a motor race or a train.

clue.text: Tramps maltreated sot in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters before it are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: In a work of fiction, vagrants abuse a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges MALTREATED SOT IN; 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ragged, shabbily dressed people.
